title: Enrollment flow likely processes directly identifying biometric data
description: A face authentication enrollment system receiving data from a user is likely to process facial images/templates that directly identify or make the user identifiable during enrollment.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not explicitly state whether the payload is a raw face image, biometric template, or additional account identifier, but face-enrollment data is typically identifying or strongly identifiable.

title: Enrollment submission may enable linkage through a unique biometric or enrollment identifier
description: Data received for face-authentication enrollment can act as a unique identifier itself (biometric template) or be tied to a unique account reference, enabling records and future authentication events to be linked to the same individual.
uncertainty_note: Assumes the enrollment data includes a biometric template, facial image, or account reference used to bind the enrollment to one person.

title: Enrollment record can become attributable evidence that the user submitted biometric data
description: The enrollment flow can create a record that a specific user submitted face data for enrollment, which may later be used as evidence that the person performed or consented to that action.
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether the system stores enrollment records with identifiers, timestamps, or audit logs.

title: Observation of enrollment communication can reveal that a user is enrolling for face authentication
description: The existence of this user-to-system enrollment communication may allow observers to detect that the individual is engaging with the face authentication enrollment process, revealing participation in the system.
uncertainty_note: Applies most clearly if network traffic, endpoint activity, or local interaction can be observed; the flow description does not specify protections or attacker model.

title: Highly sensitive biometric data may be collected during enrollment
description: Face-authentication enrollment inherently involves collection of biometric data, a highly sensitive personal data type. If more sensitive raw data is collected than strictly needed for enrollment, unnecessary disclosure risk arises.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not specify whether the system collects only a derived template or also raw images/video and auxiliary attributes.

title: User may be insufficiently aware of biometric enrollment processing
description: During enrollment, the data subject may not be fully aware of what face data is collected, how it will be transformed into templates, how long it will be retained, or with whom it may be shared.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible privacy threat for enrollment flows, but the provided context does not say whether notices, just-in-time explanations, or consent dialogs are present.

title: Biometric enrollment may rely on invalid or insufficient consent
description: Because face enrollment processes sensitive biometric personal data, collecting and processing it without valid, informed, and specific consent or another proper lawful basis may create a regulatory noncompliance risk.
uncertainty_note: This assumes a consent-based lawful ground may be required in the deployment context; the prompt gives no jurisdiction, lawful basis, or consent mechanism details.

title: Enrollment flow likely contains identifying biometric information
description: A face-authentication enrollment process sending data to a camera likely involves biometric or device-related data that can identify or single out a data subject, especially in an enrollment context where a subject is being registered.
uncertainty_note: The exact payload of DF_1 is not described. This threat assumes the flow includes enrollment instructions, subject references, or biometric capture context rather than being a purely generic trigger.

title: Enrollment communication can reveal that face enrollment is occurring
description: The communication from the enrollment system to the camera may allow observers or involved components to detect that a face-authentication enrollment session is taking place for some user or subject.
uncertainty_note: Applies if the communication is observable through logs, network metadata, or device state. The flow description does not specify transport or visibility controls.

title: Propagation of enrollment-related personal data to the camera may disclose more than necessary
description: Sending enrollment-related data from the process to the camera may expose personal data to an external entity. If the camera receives subject identifiers, session context, or other personal data beyond what is strictly needed to capture an image, this constitutes unnecessary propagation.
uncertainty_note: There is real risk because the destination is an external entity, but the exact fields in the flow are unknown.

title: Data subject may be unaware of enrollment-related processing initiated at the camera
description: Because the camera is the endpoint receiving the enrollment-related flow, the data subject may not be adequately aware that their facial data is being captured or that enrollment processing has started, especially if notices or indicators are absent or unclear.
uncertainty_note: This depends on the user interface and physical camera indicators, which are not described.

title: Enrollment flow may rely on invalid or insufficient consent
description: Face-authentication enrollment commonly involves biometric personal data. If the process sends enrollment-related information to the camera without valid consent or another proper lawful basis, the processing may be unlawful.
uncertainty_note: Lawfulness cannot be confirmed from the flow alone; this is a conditional compliance threat tied to the biometric enrollment context.

title: Enrollment data likely contains revealing facial attributes
description: The face-authentication enrollment process is likely to send facial images or derived biometric enrollment data to preprocessing. Such data can reveal identity-supporting attributes and may allow identification of the data subject.
uncertainty_note: The exact payload of DF_2 is not specified; this assumes the enrollment system sends face images and/or biometric features for preprocessing.

title: Facial enrollment data can link records through biometric similarity
description: Facial images or templates transferred for preprocessing may be linkable across sessions or datasets by assessing similarity or uniqueness of facial characteristics, enabling linkage of records belonging to the same individual.
uncertainty_note: Applies if DF_2 carries raw face images or stable biometric representations rather than fully ephemeral, non-linkable data.

title: Enrollment records may become attributable evidence of participation
description: Data sent from enrollment to preprocessing can serve as evidence that a particular individual enrolled or attempted enrollment, reducing their ability to deny participation in the process.
uncertainty_note: This depends on whether the transmitted biometric data or associated context can be tied back to a particular person or event.

title: Enrollment-to-preprocessing communication can reveal that face enrollment is occurring
description: Observation of this internal communication may allow an observer or party with access to infer that a person is undergoing face-authentication enrollment at a given time.
uncertainty_note: The threat depends on the observability of this process-to-process flow and whether it is exposed to operators, logs, or network monitoring.

title: Raw biometric data may be more sensitive than functionally necessary for preprocessing
description: If DF_2 forwards full facial images or richly detailed biometric data to the appropriateness-check and preprocessing component, the flow may disclose highly sensitive biometric information beyond the minimum needed for that stage.
uncertainty_note: The actual necessity depends on system design; some preprocessing may indeed require raw images, so this is a plausible but not certain over-collection/disclosure risk.

title: Data subject may be unaware that enrollment data is further processed for appropriateness checking
description: The data subject may not realize that biometric enrollment data is forwarded from the enrollment process to a separate preprocessing component for appropriateness checks and transformation, reducing transparency about downstream processing.
uncertainty_note: This cannot be confirmed from the flow alone; it is a common transparency risk when internal processing stages are not explained to users.

title: Transfer of biometric enrollment data may violate data minimization if broader than necessary
description: Because facial enrollment data is sensitive biometric personal data, sending more detailed or broader data than needed from enrollment to preprocessing could create a GDPR data-minimization noncompliance risk.
uncertainty_note: This depends on whether the preprocessing function truly requires the exact data sent on DF_2; the flow description alone does not prove excessiveness.

title: Face enrollment data sent for feature extraction is inherently identifying or readily identifiable
description: The enrollment process sends facial image data or equivalent raw biometric input to the ML-based feature extraction process. Facial biometric data contains revealing attributes from which the identity of the data subject may be derived, making the transferred data identifiable even if direct identifiers are not explicitly mentioned.
uncertainty_note: The flow name strongly implies biometric enrollment data is transmitted, but the exact payload is not specified; if only already-anonymized non-biometric features are sent, applicability would be reduced.

title: Feature extraction output can enable linking of enrollment records through biometric similarity
description: At the destination, ML-based feature extraction may derive embeddings or feature vectors that allow the same individual to be matched across sessions or datasets based on similarity or uniqueness. This creates linkability even without explicit identifiers.
uncertainty_note: This assumes P2 produces persistent or reusable biometric feature representations, which is typical for face-authentication pipelines but not explicitly stated.

title: ML feature extraction may constitute unnecessary analysis of sensitive biometric data
description: The destination process performs transformation and analysis on sensitive facial enrollment data. If the extraction generates richer biometric representations than strictly needed for enrollment, this introduces unnecessary processing of highly sensitive personal data.
uncertainty_note: A feature-extraction step is often functionally necessary in face-authentication systems; the threat applies specifically if the analysis or resulting representation is broader or more persistent than needed.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that enrollment facial data is forwarded to a separate ML feature-extraction component
description: This flow sends enrollment data from the enrollment system to a distinct ML-based feature extraction process. If this internal transfer and analysis are not transparent to data subjects, they may be unaware of how their biometric data is processed.
uncertainty_note: No notice or transparency context is provided, so this is a plausible but not certain threat.

title: Transfer of raw facial enrollment data for feature extraction may violate data minimization if more biometric data than needed is processed
description: Because facial biometric data is sensitive, sending raw enrollment input from P1 to P2 may process more personal data than strictly necessary unless the design minimizes what is shared and transformed for enrollment. This creates a potential GDPR data-minimization non-compliance risk.
uncertainty_note: The flow may be justified by system functionality; non-compliance depends on whether less data or a less sensitive representation could reasonably achieve the same purpose.

title: Derived features may enable linkage of records to the same individual
description: The ML-based feature extraction process may transform raw inputs into stable feature vectors or embeddings that allow records belonging to the same person to be linked across training runs, datasets, or processing stages, even if direct identifiers are absent.
uncertainty_note: Applies if extracted features are sufficiently stable and person-specific; the flow description does not specify the exact feature content.

title: Stored feature sets may remain identifiable through quasi-identifiers
description: The ML Model datastore may receive and store extracted features whose combination is distinctive enough to single out or re-identify a data subject, making the stored data identifiable even without explicit names or IDs.
uncertainty_note: This depends on whether the extracted features are high-dimensional or otherwise distinctive; the schema of the stored data is not provided.

title: Stored extracted features may become attributable evidence about a person
description: If the model store retains feature records tied directly or indirectly to a person, those records could later be used as evidence to attribute characteristics, presence, or actions to that individual, reducing plausible deniability.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation impact is plausible only if stored features can be associated with a person or event; the flow does not confirm such association.

title: Feature data may be retained in the model store longer than functionally necessary
description: Sending extracted features into the ML Model datastore creates a risk that personal data derived from individuals is kept for training, tuning, or reuse beyond the period strictly required for the stated function, increasing disclosure exposure over time.
uncertainty_note: The description names a datastore but does not state retention policy; threat is based on the common persistence implication of storing data in a datastore.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that their data is transformed into ML features for model storage
description: The feature extraction step introduces additional processing of personal data into derived ML features before storage in the model datastore. Data subjects may not understand that such derivation and storage occurs, especially when it is not obvious from the primary service interaction.
uncertainty_note: This is a general transparency risk inferred from hidden feature-engineering steps; no notice or transparency controls are described.

title: Feature extraction and storage may violate data minimization
description: The flow persists ML-extracted features from the processing component to the model datastore. If more attributes, finer-grained features, or more data points are extracted and stored than strictly necessary for model functionality, this processing would conflict with the data minimization principle.
uncertainty_note: The threat depends on whether all extracted features are necessary; the flow description does not specify necessity or feature-selection controls.

title: Biometric enrollment data can be linked to a specific person through unique identifiers
description: The enrollment process sending facial biometric enrollment data to the biometric database likely includes a stable account, subject, or template identifier so the record can be stored and retrieved later. This enables linking the stored biometric record with other records about the same individual within the system.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not explicitly list the fields carried on DF_5; this threat assumes the enrollment write includes some persistent identifier or otherwise linkable record key, which is typical for biometric enrollment.

title: Stored enrollment record is directly or indirectly identifying
description: A biometric database receiving enrollment data for face authentication is likely to store a unique reference to the enrolled person together with biometric data or template material. This makes the record identifying or readily identifiable.
uncertainty_note: The exact schema of the database record is not provided, but enrollment storage generally requires a unique subject reference to support later authentication or management.

title: Enrollment record may serve as attributable evidence of a person's participation
description: Once enrollment data is stored in the biometric database, the presence of that record can be used as evidence that a particular individual enrolled in face authentication, reducing that person's ability to deny participation or association with the system.
uncertainty_note: This depends on whether the stored record is attributable to a person through identifiers, metadata, or supporting logs; the flow alone does not confirm all such details.

title: Highly sensitive biometric data is stored in the biometric database
description: Face biometric enrollment data is sensitive personal data. Sending it from the enrollment process to persistent storage creates a data disclosure risk if raw images, rich templates, or similarly sensitive biometric artifacts are stored beyond what is strictly necessary for authentication enrollment.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not specify whether DF_5 carries raw face images, embeddings, templates, or only minimal derived data; sensitivity and excessiveness depend on that implementation choice.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that enrollment data is persistently stored in the biometric database
description: This flow represents storage of face enrollment data in a biometric database. If users are not clearly informed that their biometric enrollment information is retained in backend storage for later authentication, they may be unaware of the processing and storage of their sensitive personal data.
uncertainty_note: The existence and quality of notice, transparency, and consent mechanisms are not described, so this is a plausible but not confirmed threat.

title: Biometric enrollment storage may rely on invalid or insufficient consent
description: Because DF_5 stores face biometric enrollment data in a biometric database, there is a risk of unlawful processing if this sensitive personal data is collected and stored without valid explicit consent or another appropriate lawful basis.
uncertainty_note: This assumes a jurisdiction or regime where facial biometric enrollment is regulated as sensitive personal data and that consent or another lawful basis may be required; the flow description alone does not confirm the applicable legal basis.
